correctness.rationale: The nonempty-distinct radius-one signatures on cycles with n>=7 are equivalent to no circular 000 and no pair 00 at separation three. A seven-state transfer matrix has explicitly computed determinant D=1-tz-tz²+t²z³-t³z⁴-t³z⁵+t⁴z⁷. Its low-excess u-coefficients prove the optimum sizes and exhaustive counts; explicit H, L and exceptional E templates attain them. Pairwise exchange classification leaves only H_i--H_(i±2), H_i--L_(i+1),(i+5) and five isolated E rotations at n=15. Independent direct and transfer-trace exhaustive checks for 7<=n<=18 and template adjacency checks through n=99 succeed. Infinite assertions rest on algebra/combinatorics, not finite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Earlier literature establishes numerical minima and some constructions but the inspected fully readable primary cycle treatment does not imply a complete census and optimum-code exchange graph. The present theorem distinguishes even isolation, the connected 2n-vertex odd optimum graph and five isolated minima at n=15. Actual targeted literature and published-record searches returned no covering claim; inaccessible plausible primary texts remain an acknowledged source-level risk.

value.rationale: The exact equality cases of a classical cycle extremal problem have intrinsic combinatorial interest, and the solution-space topology (two isolated optima for even cycles, one connected 2n-state odd component, plus exactly five isolated states at n=15) is not recoverable from the published optimum cardinality. Natural orbit descriptions and exchange moves supply explicit reconfiguration paths and explain the order-fifteen resonance. This is structural rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
